## Daily demand near turning points

Daily urban water-demand forecasts can attain low average error while responding late when demand changes direction. This lag reduces their value for planning the next operating period.

The [knowledge-based bi-correction model](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2024.124508) addresses the problem in two stages. Lag-penalty attention extracts prior sequence and feature information associated with timely demand changes. A stacked LSTM produces the primary forecast. A masked weighted Markov chain then corrects selected residuals using posterior error information.

## Trend-sensitive evaluation

The study introduces mean prediction trend effectiveness to test whether a model follows changes in demand more closely than a naive forecast. Reporting this metric alongside absolute-error measures separates response timing from average numerical accuracy.

## Pressure under unobserved variation

[CritiCoder](https://doi.org/10.1109/TCSS.2023.3272330) considers macroscopic pressure when measured inputs do not explain every disturbance in a water distribution system. Its Coder models the response associated with observed variables, while the Critic changes the loss so that the remaining pressure variation can be represented as an uncertain disturbance.

The comparison tests whether CritiCoder's error increases less than conventional regression error at nodes more strongly affected by unobserved disturbances.
